title: Define degradation policy and experiment gates for interactive chat SLOs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define explicit SLO targets, a staged degradation policy, and experiment (traffic-shift) gating criteria for interactive chat endpoints. This ticket scopes acceptance criteria, measurement windows, and automated rollback triggers to be used in the next hosted and dedicated chat model rollout. The goal is to enable safe progressive traffic shifts while preserving end-user latency and availability guarantees and ensuring teams can intentionally degrade non-critical features to preserve core contract.
acceptance_criteria: SLOs defined for primary chat paths with numeric targets: p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 600ms for token-generation latency under steady-state load for typical short-turn messages (<= 256 tokens).

Availability SLO: 99.95% successful request completion (HTTP 2xx or well-formed model fallback) measured over a 30-day rolling window; error budget computed as 30-day percentage of non-successful responses.
Error budget policy: when 7-day rolling error budget burn >= 50%, freeze risky experiments; at >= 80% burn enter emergency throttle and rollback candidate variants.
Degradation bands documented: green (within SLO), amber (SLO approaching threshold: enable degraded response modes), red (breach/imminent breach: fallback to smaller model or stub responses).

Automated rollback triggers codified and testable: latency p95 spike > 2x baseline for three consecutive 1-minute buckets AND request error rate increase > 0.5% absolute over baseline -> automatic rollback of traffic to previous stable variant.
Instrumentation added: traces and spans emitted for 'chat.request', 'serving.kv_hit', 'model.variant', and 'fallback.invoked' with taggable reason codes.
Dashboards created and linked showing p50/p95/p99 token and request latency, error budget burn (7d/30d), traffic split, and per-tenant buckets.
Canary/experiment gating policy defined with explicit progressive percentages and required health checks at each step (see Rollout Plan).
Acceptance tests: synthetic load harness and dark launch checks must pass in staging: no SLO breaches for p95 under expected peak load profile and automated rollout hooks respond correctly.
metrics_definition: Request latency measured end-to-end from API ingress to final token returned; token-latency derived metric computed per request and aggregated to percentiles over 1m and 1h windows.
Success rate: responses marked successful when response schema validates and not flagged as fallback; all HTTP 5xx and internal model errors count as failures.
Error budget: 30-day rolling window. Error budget remaining = 1 - (30-day failure rate / allowed_failure_rate). Allowed failure rate for 99.95% uptime = 0.0005.
Baseline: use previous stable release baseline (last 30 days) to compute relative deltas for automated triggers. Baseline snapshots stored in S3 with daily export.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (canary dry run): 0% traffic, shadowing (dark traffic) for 48h to validate correctness and traces. Must show no increase in error patterns and <10% difference in p95 compared to baseline.
Stage 1 (canary): 1% traffic for 30 minutes -> health checks. Required: p95 within amber band, no increase in error budget burn > 10% relative. If passes, proceed.
Stage 2 (small ramp): 5% traffic for 60 minutes -> health checks. Required: p95 within green/amber and error budget burn stable. If passes, proceed.
Stage 3 (medium ramp): 20% traffic for 2 hours -> automated telemetry review and manual sign-off if any amber signals observed.
Stage 4 (wide ramp): 50% for 6 hours -> must meet p95 <= 1.1x baseline and <30% 7-day error budget burn. Otherwise, rollback to previous variant.
Stage 5 (full): 100% with post-rollout monitoring for 72 hours and retention of canary for quick rollback for 7 days.
Traffic shift pauses automatically if any stage-level health check fails; automatic rollback policy triggers if red-band conditions met.
monitoring_and_alerts: Create composite alerts: 'chat-slo-p95-breach' (p95 > 250ms sustained for 5m), 'chat-error-rate-surge' (increase in failure rate > 0.25% absolute in 5m), 'error-budget-burn-fast' (7-day burn >= 50%).
Pager duty policy: P0 escalations to on-call infra and serving runtime leads; P1 to product owner and SRE. Alerts include runbook link and recent 30m percentile charts.
Add automated annotations on rollout: every traffic shift step emits an event to the deployment timeline in the console.
test_plan: Synthetic load tests: replay representative traffic traces (short-turn and long-turn mixes) at 1.5x expected peak QPS in staging against candidate variant; measure percentile deltas and KV cache hit rates.
Dark launch correctness tests: validate end-to-end schema and hallucination/regression checks against a golden prompt set of 250 prompts covering edge cases.
Chaos checks: inject transient GPU stall and network latency in staging to verify degradation policy paths trigger and fallback works as expected.
Post-deploy canary validation suite automatically runs after each step; failure blocks progression.
decisions: Use 30-day rolling window for availability SLO and 7-day for aggressive error-budget burn detection.
Fallback hierarchy: same-architecture quantized model -> smaller fp16 model -> structured stub response with user-facing 'degraded' flag.
Automated rollback thresholds are conservative to avoid oscillation: require combined latency and error signals to trigger.
